answers.answer: 1) Select 3 Pods for 3–4 players. 2) Put the lowest-numbered in A, next in B, then alternate A/B; all start Locked. 3) Bag: 1 Blank, 4 Larvae, 1 Creeper, 1 Queen, 3 Adults plus 1 additional Adult per player (7 Adults total at four players).

1) Remove Objectives marked for higher player counts, shuffle Corporate and Personal decks separately, deal each player one of each face down. 2) At the first Encounter (first Intruder miniature appears), choose one of the two and remove the other from the game face down without looking at others’ discards. 3) Eggs are not Intruders and do not trigger this choice.
answers.evidence: Setup step 16; Critical gameplay moments—First Encounter

answers.answer: 1) Discard the Action card being played and 2 additional Action cards to pay its printed cost 2; the two Contamination cards cannot pay. 2) Contamination never substitutes for Action cards. 3) If the card has OR sections, choose one section.
answers.evidence: Actions from Action cards; Action Cost

answers.answer: 1) After finishing their own round, including the one-Action round that ends in a pass, they suffer 1 Light Wound. 2) After passing they cannot take normal Actions again that Player Phase, though Interruption remains allowed. 3) They may discard any number of hand cards when passing. 4) Later players’ rounds do not cause another wound to this already-finished Character; fire damage is checked when a Character ends their own round.

1) Entering an unexplored Room: flip it face up, set the Item count by rotating the tile so the Exploration number faces its printed counter, resolve the effect, then remove the Exploration token to the box. 2) Silence suppresses the Noise roll; Danger also suppresses it and instead moves every eligible neighboring Intruder in, or places Noise in every unmarked connected Corridor if none qualify. 3) Otherwise, if now empty, roll Noise; if another Character or Intruder is there, do not roll. 4) Slime/Fire/Malfunction/Door are placed on your Character/in the Room/in the Room/in the entry Corridor respectively. Nest and Slime Room have no Item count.
answers.evidence: Movement, Rooms, and Corridors; Exploration tokens; Noise roll

answers.answer: 1) Careful Movement costs 2 Action cards and replaces the post-move Noise roll with placing a Noise marker in a chosen Corridor connected to the destination; it also replaces automatic Silence/Danger exploration effects (Reconnaissance cancels those automatic effects too). 2) It is forbidden in Combat and if all destination-connected Corridors already have Noise. 3) Normal movement cannot cross a Closed Door; no miniature can stop in a Corridor.
answers.evidence: Basic Actions—Careful Movement; Movement, Rooms, and Corridors

answers.answer: 1) A number directing Noise to an already marked Corridor causes an Encounter. 2) Resolve by discarding all Noise in every Corridor connected to the room (including the Technical Corridors space if connected), draw a token, place its matching Intruder, and compare token number against all cards in the triggering player’s hand; fewer cards means Surprise Attack. 3) Noise is removed in this connected set; a Noise marker in Technical Corridors represents every such entrance. The drawn non-Blank token is held outside the bag until returned by a rule; Surprise Attack is against the triggering Character. 4) Contamination cards count as hand cards for the comparison.
answers.evidence: Noise roll; Technical Corridors; Encounters; Player Reference—Combat quick reference

answers.answer: 1) Danger moves all neighboring Intruders that are not in Combat with a Character into the entered Room. 2) If there are none eligible (including all being in Combat), place a Noise marker in each connected Corridor that lacks one. 3) Movement into a Character’s Room is not an Encounter; it puts them in Combat. 4) Slime turns a Silence result into Danger.

1) In an Encounter, Blank puts Noise markers in every Corridor connected to the Room and no miniature appears; return Blank to the bag. 2) If it was the last bag token, add an Adult token if available, then return Blank. 3) In ordinary bag development, Blank adds an Adult token if available, then Blank returns to the bag.

1) Both Intruders stay in their starting Room when they try the same Closed Door; they destroy that Door together. 2) A lying Destroyed Door permits movement and can never be closed again, except by Plasma Torch. 3) A Noise-triggered Intruder appearance through a Corridor ignores a Closed Door and appears anyway.

1) The Intruder disappears into the ducts: remove its miniature, discard all its Injury markers, and return its token to the bag. 2) Existing Noise on the Technical Corridors space remains. 3) Characters normally cannot use Technical Corridors, except Mechanic’s Technical Corridors Action or Technical Corridor Plans Item; Doors cannot be placed there.

1) Shoot is a Basic Action costing 1 Action card; target one Intruder in your Room, spend 1 Ammo from a Weapon in Hand, then roll. A miss does nothing. 2) Melee costs 1 Action card, draws a Contamination card to the top of your Action discard pile, and targets one Intruder in your Room; any miss gives you a Serious Wound. 3) In Shooting, the double-hit die result inflicts 2 Injuries (before Weapon modifiers); in Melee it counts as 1 Injury. Contamination cannot pay Action costs.

1) Larva dies at 1 Injury; Egg is destroyed at 1 Injury. Creeper/Adult draw one Attack card and die if blood value is no greater than current total Injuries; Queen draws two and sums blood values, dying if the sum is no greater. 2) Adult/Creeper/Queen death removes miniature and places a Carcass in the Room; Larva leaves no Carcass. 3) Any Retreat arrow changes the check to retreat instead of numerical death; Queen retreats if either of its two cards has the arrow.
answers.evidence: Combat—Intruder Injuries and death; Intruder Retreat

answers.answer: 1) Before moving, resolve one separate Intruder Attack per Intruder in the starting Room, largest first (Queen, Breeder, Adult, Larva). 2) Escape attacks target the escaping Character. 3) If they die, their Corpse stays in the Room they tried to leave. 4) If they survive, move to the chosen neighboring Room; because it is empty, roll Noise, and because unexplored, reveal it and resolve its Exploration token normally.

1) With multiple Characters, attack the one whose player has the fewest Action cards; ties go to the First Player token holder or next player in turn order. 2) Draw an Intruder Attack card; matching type symbol means resolve its effect/hit, otherwise miss; ignore blood icon for attacks. 3) Larva does not draw an Attack card: remove its miniature and put it on the target’s board, and target gains 1 Contamination card on top of their Action discard pile. If they already have a Larva, attacking Larva disappears, existing Larva stays, and only the Contamination is gained; no automatic death.

1) No: dressing suppresses a Serious Wound’s effect but it still counts toward the three-wound death limit, so any further Wound kills at 3 Serious Wounds. 2) A third Light Wound clears the Light track and causes a Serious Wound; Heal removes a Light Wound or a Dressed Serious Wound as specified. 3) On death, place a Character Corpse Object in the Room and drop all Heavy Objects there.

1) Canteen/Shower scan only Contamination cards in your hand and remove all non-Infected ones; an Infected scan places a Larva (if one already exists, Character dies and Creeper appears in Room). 2) Surgery scans all cards in hand, deck and discard, removes Infected cards and a Larva if present, then inflicts 1 Light Wound, automatically passes, and shuffles all cards including hand and remaining Contamination into Action deck; hand stays empty until next turn. 3) The summary gives no separate action-card payment detail for Surgery beyond standard Room Action cost of 2.
answers.evidence: Canteen/Shower; Surgery Room Action; Room Actions

answers.answer: 1) In a Room with uncarried Eggs, Shoot or Melee against Eggs; each Injury destroys one Egg. A missed Egg Melee causes neither Contamination nor a Wound; successful Egg Melee Contamination is unresolved in the summary. 2) Grenade destroys 2 Eggs and Molotov 1; treat target Room as if Intruder were there. 3) After each attempt roll Noise. 4) Fire in Room destroys 1 uncarried Egg per Fire Damage step, or 2 if Vulnerability to Fire is revealed. 5) Nest is destroyed once no Eggs remain on Intruder board (mark with 1 Injury).
answers.evidence: Eggs and the Nest; FAQ—Vulnerability to Fire

answers.answer: 1) Pay 2 Action cards for Evacuation Section A/B Room Action; the Section must have an Unlocked Pod with a free Character space. Entry is barred if an Intruder or Malfunction is present in Section. 2) Roll Noise first; an Intruder appearing or being present makes entry fail. 3) Pod capacity is 2 Characters; Heavy Objects do not use Character spaces. 4) After boarding, launch immediately or wait/pass the current turn; in later Player Phases choose at the start of your first round: keep waiting and pass, launch, or exit free into the Section and take a full two-Action round. Waiting keeps you present for bag-development Noise; an Intruder appearing in Section returns Pod occupants to its Room; a Malfunction while already waiting still permits wait/launch/exit but prevents new entry.

1) Victory checks: Engines, Coordinates, Contamination, Objectives. 2) If 2 or 3 Engines are Damaged, everything aboard dies, including sleepers and Intruders; launched Pods are away. 3) If destination is not Earth, Hibernatorium sleepers die, but ship and Intruders survive; Quarantine Objective survives at Mars. Ship-to-Earth/Mars Objective also requires correct Coordinates and at least 2 Working Engines. 4) Contamination: scan all cards; if any Infected, shuffle all cards and draw 4, where any Contamination card kills; a Larva skips scan and triggers that test directly. No Larva and no Infected cards means no four-card draw. 5) Pod passengers still face Contamination and Objective checks.
answers.evidence: Victory Check; Objective types; Escape Pods

answers.answer: 1) Use basic board side. Shuffle Room 2 tiles face down, place on all marked 2 slots and return extras unseen; do same for all Room 1 tiles. Shuffle Exploration tokens face down, put one on each Room, return extras. 2) Place one random Coordinates card face down by Cockpit; Destination marker on B; Time marker on green space. 3) For each Engine, shuffle its Working and Damaged tokens face down, stack on slot, top is true status. 4) Put 5 Eggs and 3 random Weakness cards face down on Intruder board.

1) Random Help cards numbered to player count assign Player Numbers and choice order. Shuffle Draft cards; player 1 draws 2, keeps 1, shuffles other back, then next player in order. 2) Each gets board, miniature in Hibernatorium, shuffled 10 Action cards, Starting Weapon in a Hand slot loaded to its capacity, two Quest Items horizontal/inactive, and discard space; Player 1 takes First Player token. 3) Blue Character Corpse starts in Hibernatorium. Quest Items are not usable at start; activate by fulfilling their card condition.

1) At each Player Phase start, everyone draws to 5 Action cards (Cabins may make 6); after drawing pass First Player token left except first game turn. 2) If Action deck is empty when drawing, shuffle discard into a new deck then draw. 3) Used Action and Contamination cards go to personal Action discard; normal discards are face up. Item/Event/Attack/Wound piles have discard spaces; cards face up.

1) Event Phase order: advance Time (and active Self-Destruct), Intruders in Combat attack, Fire Damage to Intruders, resolve Event card (movement then card effect), bag development. 2) On Event movement, only Intruders with the shown symbol and not in a Room with any Characters move; card number selects matching Corridor, and entering Technical Corridors removes them to bag. Then resolve effect. 3) Event deck exhaustion: shuffle Event discard into new deck. Intruder Attack deck exhaustion: shuffle its discard into a new deck.

1) Larva draw: remove that token and add Adult to bag. 2) Creeper: remove token, add Breeder. 3) Adult: return token immediately before all players roll Noise in order (skip Combat), and an Encounter can draw that same token. 4) Breeder: same Noise rolls, then return token. 5) Queen: if Characters in Nest, place Queen and resolve Encounter; otherwise add Egg to Intruder board; return Queen token. 6) Blank: add Adult if available, return Blank. 7) Next turn begins only after this bag step and all resulting Encounters/Surprise Attacks finish.

1) Trying to place a ninth Fire marker or ninth Malfunction marker ends game as ship explodes/loses hull integrity. Extra marker on a Room already marked does nothing; discarded markers return to pool. 2) When hull is lost, all Characters aboard (including hibernating) and everything aboard including Intruders die.
answers.evidence: End of the game; Fire, Malfunction, Doors…

answers.answer: 1) Malfunction disables that Room’s Action and its Computer; Search still works. 2) It cannot be placed in Nest, Room Covered in Slime, or an unexplored Room. 3) It does not change true Engine token/status; Hibernatorium malfunction does not affect already-hibernating Characters.

1) Normal Item cards in Inventory holders are hidden; others see only backs/colors. No Inventory size limit; show any Item when used. 2) Heavy Items/Objects are public and occupy one of two Hand slots, max two; heavy Items found by Search are handled as Hand contents without separate Pick Up Action. Add Items attach to another card and act as one; Duct Tape combines two Heavy Items in one slot, never Objects. 3) Heavy Objects are Egg, Character Corpse, Intruder Carcass; must be carried in Hand slots.

1) Drop Items are discarded/lost; dropped Objects remain in Room. 2) Drop for free any time during your turn, no Action. 3) Found Weapons have 1 Ammo; a Weapon cannot exceed its printed capacity. Starting Weapon is loaded to its Ammo capacity.
answers.evidence: Items and Objects—Sources, Heavy Items, Drop; Crew setup

answers.answer: 1) Search Action card selects deck matching Room background color (white Room lets you choose Red/Yellow/Green); Blue Crafted Items are never found by search. 2) Draw 2, keep 1, put rejected card face down at bottom of deck. 3) Each Search lowers Room Item Counter by 1; at zero cannot search (except Scout Scavenging). Special Rooms have no Search; Nest and Slime Room explicitly prohibit any Search.

1) Craft Item Basic Action costs one Action card plus discarding 2 Item cards whose blue Component icons match the Crafted Item’s 2 gray icons. 2) The result card must be available; crafted deck may be inspected any time. 3) Recipes: Antidote flame + medical cross; Taser battery/lightning + screwdriver/tool; Flamethrower flame + screwdriver/tool; Molotov flame + folded cloth/fabric.

1) Only Trade initiator spends the Action; any Characters in the Room may trade among themselves, and all choose whether to agree. 2) Giving an Item/Object for nothing is allowed; Ammo cannot be exchanged. 3) Heavy Items found through Search do not need a separate Pick Up Action; that action is for Objects.
answers.evidence: Basic Actions—Trade; Pick Up Heavy Object

answers.answer: 1) Research/analyse the corresponding Object: Character Corpse, Intruder Carcass, or Egg, in the Laboratory. 2) Reveal corresponding Weakness face up on Intruder board; Object stays and is not consumed, effect benefits all players. 3) Discover Weakness objective requires that the corresponding Object be researched in Laboratory by anyone before game end, not personally by you.

1) Room Action costs 2 Action cards; must be in that Room, out of Combat, and no Malfunction there. 2) A Computer icon itself has no general effect stated; Malfunction makes a Room’s Computer unavailable. 3) Fire does not prevent Room Actions or Searching.
answers.evidence: Room Actions; Malfunction markers; Fire markers

answers.answer: 1) Armory adds 2 Ammo to one of your Energy Weapons. 2) It never affects Classic Weapons and cannot exceed weapon capacity.

1) Emergency Room offers exactly one of: dress all Serious Wounds; heal one Dressed Serious Wound; or heal all Light Wounds. 2) Dressing flips Serious Wound face down, suppressing effect but not removing/counting it. 3) Duplicate Serious Wound effects do not stack, though multiple cards remain harder to clear.
1) Send Signal means place a Status marker on your Character board’s Signal space. 2) It is used only for Objectives. 3) Comms Room is always aboard in normal game.

1) Choose any Room; discard its Fire marker if present. 2) All Intruders there flee in random directions, drawing an Event card per Intruder. 3) Works even if the chosen Room had no Fire, so it can scatter Intruders anyway.

1) Generator Action starts Self-Destruct at first green space or stops it by removing marker; a new sequence restarts from green. 2) Advance one space whenever Time advances. 3) At first yellow, cannot stop and all Pods automatically unlock; they may be re-Locked, but later yellow spaces do not unlock again. 4) Final skull space explodes ship. 5) If hyperspace jump occurs while active, ship is considered destroyed. 6) Characters cannot start it while anyone hibernates; Coolant Leak Event can.

1) Target any one OTHER Yellow Room whose connected Corridors have no Destroyed Doors. 2) Immediately close every Door around it and put Airlock Procedure token there. 3) If all doors remain closed at end of current Player Phase, everything there dies and Fire is removed. 4) Opening any door first cancels it.
1) At start of a new turn, a Character in Cabins with no Intruders there draws one extra Action card, for 6 instead of 5. 2) Malfunction disables it. 3) It is passive, not a paid Room Action.

1) Yes. Command Center chooses any Room and opens/closes any selected Doors in connected Corridors, so may individually choose a mix. Destroyed Door is lying token and can never close again (except Plasma Torch), so cannot be closed by Command Center.
1) Engine Control Room checks status of all three Engines; it cannot change them. 2) It works even if an Engine Room has a Malfunction.

1) Hatch Control System flips one Escape Pod token to Locked or Unlocked. 2) Monitoring Room secretly looks at any one unexplored Room tile and its Exploration token, then replaces them; you may lie about what you saw.
answers.evidence: Player Reference—Hatch Control System; Monitoring Room

answers.answer: 1) No Action to acquire Slime: entering automatically puts Slime on your board. 2) No Item count is set there, Malfunction cannot be placed there, and Slime cannot stack (max one). 3) Shower removes your Slime but does not extinguish Fire.
answers.evidence: Player Reference—Room Covered With Slime/Shower; Slime marker

answers.answer: 1) Cockpit lets you secretly look at Coordinates and remember/lie about them, or move Destination marker. 2) Destination means the marker’s selected destination on the Destination Track. 3) Cannot Set Destination with Intruder in Cockpit or change it once anyone hibernates. 4) The summary says check is secret; it does not state that other players are shown the card.

1) Check Engine secretly looks at top token and you may lie. 2) Repair/Break via Repairs Action or Tools Item secretly examine both tokens and restack in any order; need not say whether repaired, but must announce if order changed. 3) No prior check needed; works even with Malfunction in Engine Room.

1) Hibernation is legal only when Time marker on a blue space. 2) Try: Noise roll; if Intruder appears or is present, fails; otherwise remove miniature and safely hibernate, out of game until end. 3) Summary does not specify a separate fatal failure consequence beyond attempt fails. 4) Later ship destruction/endgame checks can kill sleepers; Malfunction in Hibernatorium does not affect already-hibernating Character.
answers.evidence: Critical gameplay moments—Hibernation opens; Player Reference—Hibernatorium; Malfunction markers

answers.answer: 1) Time reaching final red space jumps ship immediately; awake Characters aboard die from g-force, hibernators are spared that effect, Intruders unharmed. 2) If last alive non-hibernating Character dies, hibernates, or launches, end game: advance active Self-Destruct to final red and resolve, or if inactive move Time to final red and resolve. 3) Normal jump does not kill Intruders; active Self-Destruct during jump still means ship destroyed.
answers.evidence: End of the game; Self-Destruct sequence

answers.answer: 1) Characters cannot directly attack one another due to anti-aggression implants. 2) Indirect harm is possible, e.g. lock another in burning Room, start Self-Destruct with crew aboard, or throw Grenade into Room with other crew.

1) If all eight Adult models on board, remove all Adults not in Combat and return their tokens to bag if possible, then place one in Encounter Room. If all eight are in Combat, summary says procedure is not explained and needs authoritative clarification. 2) Intruder entering unexplored Room by movement remains there; do not flip Room or reveal Exploration token.
answers.evidence: Encounters—Adult overflow; Intruders in unexplored Rooms

answers.answer: 1) Small curled symbol hits Larva or Creeper only; otherwise miss. Larger curved symbol hits Larva, Creeper, or Adult; otherwise miss. 2) In Melee these results mirror shooting; against an ineligible target they miss, and any melee miss causes attacker 1 Serious Wound.

1) No four-card draw: with no Larva and no Infected card after scanning all Contamination cards in deck/discard/hand, survivor passes check without drawing. Cards are scanned, not removed merely for being non-Infected by this endgame test. 2) Launched Pod occupants still undergo Objective check.

1) Antidote = flame + medical cross. 2) Taser = battery/lightning + screwdriver/tool. 3) Flamethrower = flame + screwdriver/tool. 4) Molotov Cocktail = flame + folded cloth/fabric. These are component icons, not assumed Item card names.

1) In Combat whenever Character and Intruder share a Room; Eggs are not Intruders and do not count. 2) “In Combat only” requires that state; “Out of Combat only” requires no Intruder in your Room. 3) Unmarked Actions/Items can work in either state subject to their other requirements. Basic Actions in Combat limited to Shoot, Melee and Basic Movement as Escape; no Trade, Craft, Pick Up Object or Quest activation; Room Actions forbidden.

1) For “Player X’s Character cannot survive,” X must be dead at game end, not hibernating or escaped; you need not personally kill them. 2) “Only survivor” means no other Character may survive. 3) Regardless, your own Character must survive (Pod or hibernation) and fulfill own Objective.

1) If Door pool empty, move any Door token from elsewhere on board. 2) Open is no token, Closed is standing token, Destroyed is lying token; Destroyed cannot close again except Plasma Torch. 3) Max one Door per Corridor; never in Technical Corridors.
1) First Character death automatically unlocks all Escape Pods by flipping tokens. 2) They may subsequently be Locked/Unlocked normally through the rest of game.

1) Storage Room Action draws 2 from a chosen Red/Yellow/Green Item deck, keeps 1, rejected card goes face down to bottom of that same deck. It works repeatedly even at Item Counter zero. 2) Normal Room Action costs 2 Action cards, requires presence, no Combat and no Malfunction; Search Action card is separately limited by counter.
answers.evidence: Player Reference—Storage; Storage FAQ; Room Actions

answers.answer: 1) In Nest, perform its Room Action: take one Egg token from Intruder board, then make a Noise roll. 2) Standard Room Action costs 2 Action cards and usual Room restrictions apply. 3) A previously dropped Egg is an ordinary Heavy Object in your Room, taken with Pick Up Heavy Object Basic Action (1 Action card); it is not an Intruder-board egg and picking up does not invoke Nest Action.
answers.evidence: Player Reference—Nest; Pick Up Heavy Object

answers.answer: 1) After paying its printed Action-card cost and showing/using it, discard a One Use Only Item card.
answers.evidence: Actions from Item cards; Item Action cost

answers.answer: 1) A launched Escape Pod occupant counts as arriving on Earth. 2) This does not prove the ship reached Earth: Pods are already away, while ship Coordinates are separately checked.
1) Yes. While waiting, you remain treated as present in the Section for bag-development Noise rolls.
1) Yes, if already waiting you may continue waiting, launch, or exit; Malfunction blocks only new Pod entry.
answers.evidence: Escape Pods—Malfunction appears in the Section while you wait

answers.answer: 1) Escape resolves one separate attack per Intruder in the Room, in descending size order: Queen, Breeder, Adult, then Larva.
1) Yes. If an Event says remove itself from the game, remove it even when its other effect cannot resolve.
1) Return drawn Adult token immediately before all players roll Noise in order, skipping Characters in Combat. 2) An Encounter triggered by those rolls may draw that same token from the bag.
1) Normally a retreating Intruder encountering Closed Door destroys it and stays. 2) With The Way of Moving Weakness, affected non-Breeder/non-Queen instead does nothing at that Door.
1) No. Hand Serious Wound does not increase Basic Shoot cost; its effect does not apply to that Basic Action.
1) Vulnerability to Fire adds 1 Injury per damage instance (x+1). 2) A Flamethrower double-crosshair hit deals 3 Injuries.
1) Attacking Larva is removed from board and disappears; existing Larva remains on Character. 2) Character gains 1 Contamination card and is not automatically killed by that Larva attack.
1) Sleeper takes no later Fire wounds in Hibernatorium. 2) Ship destruction and endgame survival checks can still kill them.
answers.evidence: FAQ—sleeper takes no later Fire wounds

answers.answer: 1) Yes. Coolant Leak Event can start Self-Destruct while someone hibernates. 2) A Character using Generator cannot start it while any Character hibernates.
1) Discarded/dead Intruder tokens return to unused token pool and remain reusable; they are not permanently removed.
1) Fire can be placed in unexplored Rooms. 2) Malfunction cannot be placed in unexplored Rooms.
1) First new Light Wound (the third total) clears Light track and becomes one Serious Wound; the second new Light Wound then leaves 1 Light Wound.
1) On Character death, Heavy Objects drop in the Room. 2) Item cards disappear from the game.
1) No. Pods automatically unlock when Self-Destruct first reaches yellow; they may be re-Locked, and later yellow spaces do not unlock them again.
1) Yes. Ship destruction fulfills objectives to kill Queen or destroy Nest. 2) That alone does not make your Character a winner: your Character must survive and fulfill their Objective.
1) No; empty Actions with no meaningful game-state change, including deliberately starting Trade with no intent to exchange, are disallowed. 2) Genuine negotiations may honestly end without a trade.
1) Quest activation is a Basic Action printed on the card. 2) Forbidden in Combat. 3) Allowed in a Malfunctioning Room.

1) Basic Combat Actions: Shoot, Melee, Basic Movement as Escape. 2) Cannot Trade, Craft, Pick Up Object, or activate Quest Item in Combat; Room Actions also forbidden. 3) Actions/Items marked for combat state obey their label; unmarked card or Item Actions can be used in or out subject to requirements.
answers.evidence: Actions—In Combat/Out of Combat; Basic Actions

answers.answer: 1) Soldier can use Covering Fire for themselves alone. 2) Both Characters move in the direction each chooses, then make one Noise roll. 3) Any Encounter compares surprise against Soldier.
1) Full Auto removes all Ammo, then performs one Shoot Action. 2) Damage adds the Shoot result, half of discarded Ammo rounded down, and Assault Rifle’s +1 bonus.

1) You may see the Intruder Attack card before choosing whether to use Nerves of Steel. 2) It can protect Soldier when another Character triggered Surprise Attack, but only Soldier benefits; others still suffer effects such as Frenzy.
1) Careful Movement’s chosen Noise placement replaces automatic Danger/Silence Exploration results. 2) Reconnaissance cancels those automatic results too.
1) Captain cannot use Order while personally in Combat. 2) Intercom may make another Character Move out of Combat, but normal Escape rules/attacks apply.
1) Motivation with active Intercom affects all Characters in Rooms with a Computer and all Characters in Captain’s Room.
1) Door Exploration token is ignored when entering via Technical Corridors Action or Technical Corridor Plans because the entry Corridor cannot be determined.

1) No. Interruption requires being in the same Room as the Character taking the interrupted Action, so a remote Intercom Order cannot be interrupted from elsewhere. 2) Passing does not bar Interruption; it remains allowed.
1) No. Empty hand after completing two Actions does not automatically make you pass; wait for next round to pass. 2) That extra round can incur another Fire or Bleeding effect.
1) No: if no Larva before Rest, several Infected scans place just one Larva and cannot kill merely from multiplicity. 2) Rest can be fatal if Larva was already on board before the Action.
1) Roll Noise in your own Room, not in the Nest, when throwing Grenade/Molotov at Nest Eggs from another Room.
1) No. Object itself must be in Laboratory for research/Analyse, regardless of Scientist’s location or carrying it elsewhere.

1) Yes. Storage Room Action can be repeated at zero counter, paying normal cost and observing Room restrictions. 2) Ordinary Search Action card is limited by counter: at zero Room is emptied and cannot be searched, except Scout Scavenging.
1) Two Eggs are destroyed per Fire Damage step when Nest has Fire and Vulnerability to Fire is discovered.
1) No. Once taken from Intruder board, Egg is a normal Heavy Object; dropping it in Nest does not restore Nest Egg total/hit points.
1) Each affected player chooses one Action card from their own hand and discards it.
1) Yes. Medkit and Bandages may be used on other Characters.
1) No direct reload of another Character’s Weapon. 2) Trade Energy Charge to them so they use it during their own round to recharge.
1) No Larva is placed by Alcohol’s Infected scan; instead you gain a new Contamination card.
1) Yes. Adding Extended Magazine or Auto Loader to a used/empty Energy Weapon immediately grants extra Ammo.
1) Newly Crafted Flamethrower starts fully loaded, not with one Ammo.
1) No. Hand Serious Wound does not affect Scout’s Motion Scanner because it is a unique reaction, not an Item Action.

1) Antidote scans all Contamination cards in hand, deck and discard; removes all Infected from game; gains 1 new Contamination; reshuffles that new card with non-Infected scanned Contamination and Action cards except cards retained in hand. 2) Then pass; you may keep hand cards. 3) Surgery also scans all zones, removes infected and a Larva, but has no new Contamination; it costs 1 Light Wound and forces pass while shuffling entire hand and remaining cards into Action deck.
1) Exploration places Slime marker on your Character board; Fire and Malfunction markers in the entered Room; Door token in the Corridor by which you entered.

1) Each Intruder in burning Room suffers 1 Injury during Fire Damage step. 2) This is after Intruder Attack step and before Event resolution. 3) Summary says put injury marker and check Injury Effect after injuries, so death/retreat check follows; no separate special extra check is described beyond normal Injury Effect.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure—Event Phase; Combat—Intruder Injuries and death

answers.answer: 1) No. Nest and Room Covered With Slime explicitly prohibit any Search Action, even though ordinary Room tiles may be searched.
